Subject: Privacy onboarding — SSQ + subprocessors

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're starting our vendor onboarding checklist for HealthWave's new AI integrations and need answers to a few privacy/security items before procurement can sign off. Primary asks:

- Completed security questionnaire focused on PII handling (attached spreadsheet).
- Current subprocessor roster and which subprocessors have access to raw PII or tokenized identifiers.
- Clarification on cross-border transfers and legal mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy, or other).
- Evidence of KMS separation and key custody model for customer data.

I've attached a blank copy of our SSQ (HealthWave_SSQ.xlsx) with the questions we prioritize. Can you confirm who on your side will own each section and estimated turnaround? Procurement is targeting a completion window of next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2028-07-14T15:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy onboarding — SSQ + subprocessors

Claire,

Thanks — quick answers inline and next steps. I started filling the attached SSQ and added notes where we need HealthWave clarification. Key points up front:

1) Subprocessor roster: attached as redwood_subprocessors_v3.csv. Columns include role, host country, whether the subprocessor has access to raw PII, and justification for use. Our policy: most GPU and storage partners do not receive unredacted PII — only anonymized or tokenized identifiers unless the customer grants explicit access.

2) KMS & key custody: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and customer HSM). For HealthWave's Dedicated or Private deployment we can configure customer-controlled keys; for hosted accounts we offer envelope encryption and a bring-your-own-key option for higher tiers. I've referenced our KMS attestation packet in the Drive link.

3) Cross-border transfers: We default to SCCs for transfers from the EU. For US->non-EU transfers we rely on contractual safeguards and can add specific routing (regional model pinning) to avoid transfers where required. If you have EU residency constraints for HealthWave users, we recommend our Dedicated or Private deployment.

4) Evidence: attaching our SOC 2 Type II summary and a PII handling diagram (dataflow_v2.png) for your intake. Full reports can be shared under an NDA or via your secure portal.

I tagged follow-up items in the SSQ where we need the exact data categories HealthWave will send to the model (PHI? PII types? hashed identifiers?). That will determine allowable subprocessors and retention windows.

Next actions:
- Tessa: please upload the redline DPA to the Drive and flag any clauses HealthWave must have.
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the current DPA redline covers SCC language and if we need to propose an additional transfer appendix?

Thanks,

Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_v3.csv; dataflow_v2.png; SOC2_Summary.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Wong <claire.w@healthwave.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy onboarding — SSQ + subprocessors

Claire — quick legal note and attachments.

Attached is a redline of the DPA (dpa_redline_v1.pdf) addressing the transfer mechanisms and subprocessor approval workflow. Highlights:
- We can incorporate SCCs where necessary and will provide a transfer appendix for EU-resident data.
- Subprocessor onboarding: we maintain an internal approval workflow and will provide a 30-day notice for new subprocessors that access raw PII. For highly regulated categories (healthcare PHI), we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments and the option to approve subprocessors via a separate exhibit.
- KMS: we will commit to BYOK options on Dedicated/Private; for hosted tiers BYOK is available on our enterprise plans (we've noted this in §4.3).

Please review the redline and let us know which items HealthWave would like to escalate to their legal or security teams. Happy to join a call next week to walk through the redline line-by-line.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_redline_v1.pdf
